chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recites the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) before bending his legs from the obligatory Salat, Allah will forgive him, and let him begin with the Takbir.'

key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ: Glorification (specifically referring to the Tasbih of Fatima)
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ الزَّهْرَاءِ: Fatima al-Zahra, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.يَثْنِيَ رِجْلَيْهِ: Bending his legs (rising from the sitting position in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice and reward for reciting the Tasbih of Fatima after obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi prescribes the recitation of the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra (Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar) immediately after the final Tashahhud but before the concluding Takbir, a timing that distinguishes it from post-prayer dhikr recited after rising. It emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of this specific supplication, linking it directly to divine forgiveness, while clarifying the ritual sequence by noting that the formal prayer concludes with the Takbir before the supplication begins. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and exemplary role of the Ahl al-Bayt in daily worship.
